original_question: Given a positive integer d, does there exist an algebraic group G with Cayley degree Cay(G) > d? If so, does there exist a simple algebraic group with Cay(G) > d?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 10: "Given a d ∈ N, is there G such that Cay(G) > d? Is there a simple such G?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual open problem. It correctly asks for arbitrarily large Cayley degree, quantifies by a given positive integer d, and separately asks whether the same phenomenon can occur for a simple group. That is exactly the content of Section 2, Problem 10.
missing_details: The paper works under the ambient convention that all algebraic varieties are over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero.
In Section 2, G is not an arbitrary algebraic group: the setup is a connected reductive algebraic group G, with the simple case meaning a connected simple algebraic group in this same setting.
The notation Cay(G) must be defined: it is the minimum of the degrees of dominant G-equivariant rational maps G ↛ Lie(G).
The two G-actions used in that definition are part of the setup: G acts on Lie(G) via the adjoint representation and on G by conjugation.
The paper notes that such dominant G-equivariant rational maps always exist, so Cay(G) is well defined before Problem 10 is posed.
The official formulation asks the two existence questions independently; it does not phrase the second one conditionally as "If so".

The draft does not indicate that this is the more specific existence problem of Problem 10, rather than the broader neighboring Problem 7 asking to determine all Cayley degrees of connected simple algebraic groups.
refined_question: Working over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero, let G be a connected reductive algebraic k-group, with G acting on itself by conjugation and on Lie(G) by the adjoint action. Define the Cayley degree Cay(G) to be the minimum of deg(φ), where φ ranges over dominant G-equivariant rational maps φ: G ↛ Lie(G) (equivalently, deg(φ) = [k(G):φ^*k(Lie(G))]). Given a positive integer d, does there exist such a group G with Cay(G) > d? Moreover, does there exist a connected simple algebraic k-group G with Cay(G) > d?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 2, Problem 10, not the broader Problem 7. In the paper, Popov first fixes the ambient field convention, then in Section 2 introduces the Cayley setup for connected reductive algebraic groups, defines Cayley groups and Cayley degree, recalls the known bounds, and only then asks exactly the "Given d ∈ N ..." existence question. So the faithful refinement is to keep Problem 10's scope and merely make its implicit setup explicit.
